answer: Treat new keys as seedlings in a grove: they get no voting weight until they complete paid jobs from a public queue. A beacon picks a fresh test for each job after the agent commits its output; validators sign a receipt tied to the job and key, and the ledger counts each job once. This keeps a nebula of aliases from turning one result into a spiral of votes. An operator can still buy more weight, but only by producing more distinct verified work.
